replication.target_description: Primary replication compares college students’ Q1 beliefs and Q2 revealing information across specific-lie, several-lies, and general conditions, for behavioral versus contextual information. The officer/community and verbal-contradiction/active-strategy description does not uniquely identify a replication test.

es.location: p. 332, Frequencies; see also p. 331 Data analysis and p. 333 Dichotomous data/Table 3

notes: Identity verified from the supplied canonical text: title Do people detect deception the way they think they do? Replication and extensions; Nuria Sánchez and Jaume Masip; Psicothema 2020, Vol. 32, No. 3, 329-336; doi: 10.7334/psicothema2019.405. This is a primary empirical report with Method, Results, Discussion and references, spanning all eight printed pages, not an abstract-only parse or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Only replication es_value_r is assigned; all other fields are placeholders. The neutral description concerns officers versus community members, verbal contradictions, and active detection strategies; the supplied replication is a college-student study with several possible questionnaire/information-type tests. Page 332 does not identify one unique target from this description. Preserve candidate statistics without selecting by numeric matching or page order. Candidate printed test statistics on p. 332 (frequency data): questionnaire main effect ATS (1) = 9.92, p = .002; information-type main effect ATS (1) = 129.31, p < .001; Questionnaire × Information-Type interaction ATS (1) = 33.50, p < .001; three-way interaction ATS (1) = 2.68, p = .078. Alternative dichotomous analysis on p. 333: questionnaire ATS (1) = 25.36, p < .001; information type ATS (1) = 98.55, p < .001; two-way interaction ATS (1) = 63.76, p < .001; three-way interaction ATS (1) = 0.87, p = .416. Table 3 also reports multiple pairwise Z scores for frequency data. No unique test or standardisation is inferred; no effect conversion or N derivation performed.
